abstract: Alternative splicing generates transcript isoforms with distinct tissue-expression patterns, but resources integrating transcript distribution, abundance consistency, and relative abundance remain limited. We developed MIsoTEx (Mammalian Isoform Tissue Expression Resource), a database and expression-pattern-based classification framework for protein-coding iso-mRNAs in human, mouse, and rat. RNA-seq datasets from GTEx, ARCHS4, and newly curated datasets from SRA were used to construct catalogs, following stringent selection of normal adult tissue samples. Ubiquitously detected iso-mRNAs were classified as uniformly abundant (UUni) or variably abundant (UVar), while tissue-associated iso-mRNAs were classified as tissue-predominant (TPred), tissue-exclusive (TExcl), tissue-poor (TPoor), or tissue-absent (TAbsn). These classes were further divided into five relative-abundance sub-classes, with confidence scores assigned to tissue-associated classifications. MIsoTEx contains ~147 000 protein-coding iso-mRNAs and supports gene- and transcript-based queries, tissue-pattern searches, cross-species comparison of orthologs with concordant expression, and analysis of user-supplied expression data to identify candidate control iso-mRNAs. Comparisons with independent RNA-seq, RT-PCR, and published expression datasets provided support for aspects of the classification framework. Functional enrichment analysis revealed distinct biological associations among selected expression-based categories. MIsoTEx facilitates transcript-level exploration of mammalian tissue-expression patterns and helps identify candidate reference iso-mRNAs for experimental evaluation. The database can be accessed using the link: https://resources.ibab.ac.in/MIsoTEx/.
